findings.title: retryCount cleanup condition is not scoped to unscheduled SMS reminders
findings.body: The new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method` or `scheduled` filter, so `deleteMany` removes every WorkflowReminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) or whether it was already scheduled. The intent is to drop only SMS reminders that repeatedly failed to schedule. As written, unrelated reminders can be silently deleted, and already-scheduled reminders that have a referenceId can be removed while Twilio still holds the scheduled message. The retry condition should be combined with `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and `scheduled: false`.

findings.title: Unguarded update in catch block can abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The retryCount update added in the `catch` block is not wrapped in its own try/catch. If that database update throws (connection error, record already deleted by the cleanup step, etc.), the exception propagates out of the `for` loop. All remaining unscheduled reminders in the batch are skipped for this run and the handler fails. One failing reminder should not stop processing of the others.

findings.title: Retry threshold does not match the PR description
findings.body: The description says the reminder is deleted after scheduling fails twice. The condition `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` deletes when retryCount reaches 2, which is after two failures, so that part matches. However, the cleanup runs at the start of the next cron pass, so a reminder is actually removed on the third run. The comment above the deleteMany still only says it deletes past-dated reminders, which no longer describes the code. The comment should be updated to mention the retry-based deletion.
